lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p36 - Talk about the pictures.

details: Talk about the pictures activates vocabulary recall. Students identify the various meal combinations in the review section to ensure they know the names of all the food items.
Look for accurate naming of the foods shown on the plates (e.g., "Fish and potatoes," "Chicken and pasta") when prompted.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p36 - Listen and tick.

details: Listen and tick assesses auditory comprehension. Students listen to the descriptions of the meals and select the correct image by ticking the box.
Look for attentive listening and marking the correct meal combination that matches the audio description.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p36 - Complete the chart for you. Then ask and answer.

details: Complete the chart allows for personalization and social interaction. Students tick their own food preferences in the "Me" column, then interview a partner using "What would you like?" to complete the "My friend" column.
Look for correct use of the question form and recording the friend's answers by ticking the correct boxes in the second column.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p36 - Talk about your choices.

details: Talk about your choices assesses speaking fluency. Students present the results of their survey to the class or teacher, using sentences like "I'd like pizza" and "My friend would like chicken."
Look for clear pronunciation of the food vocabulary and correct use of the "would like" structure to report findings.
